claims.text: The low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi arise from deformation dominated by easy dislocation glide.
Deformation of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is accompanied by rapid dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery prevents substantial dislocation accumulation and work hardening.
Limited dislocation accumulation explains the combination of favorable plasticity and limited strengthening during deformation.
The applicable initial material is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution state.
Changing strain rate and temperature can modulate the extent of dynamic recovery.
Ambient-temperature deformation at moderate strain rates produces high or prevalent dynamic recovery.
Higher strain rates and/or lower temperatures suppress dynamic recovery relative to the ambient, moderate-strain-rate baseline.
The relevant structural mediator is the evolving intragranular dislocation density and configuration.
CoCrFeNiTi in the stated state has high intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
CoCrFeNiTi in the stated state has low lattice friction that permits easy dislocation slip.
Rapid dynamic recovery continuously reorganizes dislocations and limits their buildup.
Easy slip and recovery-mediated limitation of dislocation buildup reduce work hardening, hardness, and strength while retaining plasticity and machinability.
At ambient temperature and moderate strain rates, deformation will exhibit low strain hardening and only a minimal increase in dislocation density.
Higher strain rates or lower temperatures will produce greater dislocation accumulation than the baseline.
Higher strain rates or lower temperatures will increase work hardening, hardness, and strength relative to the baseline.
The hypothesis is restricted to equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi without precipitates and to loading conditions that do not induce phase changes or secondary-phase formation.
Failure of increased strain rate or reduced temperature to increase dislocation accumulation, work hardening, and hardness relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
